name: Zim Stocks Part 3: How You Get Paid

segments.title: HOW YOU GET PAID
segments.say: Zim stocks, part three of four. There are two ways shares pay you. Let's break them down. How you actually make money. There are two ways: the share price going up, and dividends.

segments.title: WAY 1: PRICE GROWTH
segments.note: AfricanFinancials YTD to 19 Nov 2026. Before trading costs. Past gains don't repeat on schedule.

items.text: Put into Padenga on the VFEX in January

segments.say: Way one is price growth. Say you put 100 US dollars into Padenga on the VFEX in January. By the 19th of November, it would be worth about 225 dollars, before costs. The same 100 dollars in Caledonia Mining would be worth about 78. Same market, same year, very different results. That's why research matters.

segments.title: WAY 2: DIVIDENDS
segments.note: Example: CBZ Holdings final dividend, AfricanFinancials dividend table.

items.sub: CBZ: 17 Apr 2026, 1.61 US cents a share

items.text: Own the shares BEFORE this date

segments.say: A dividend is a share of the company's profit, paid in cash. Here's a real example. CBZ declared a final dividend of 1.61 US cents a share in April. To get it, you had to own the shares before the ex-dividend date, the 7th of May. The money was paid on the 15th. Buy on or after the ex-date, and you miss it.

segments.title: THE DIVIDEND TRAP

items.text: A very high yield can be a warning sign

items.sub: so the same payout looks bigger
look at earnings, not just the yield

segments.say: Now, the dividend trap. A very high dividend yield can look amazing, but often it's high because the share price has crashed. Always ask: can the company's profits keep paying this? A dividend can be cut at any time. Dividends are also taxed before you receive them, so ask your broker what rate applies to you.
